Hi Naomi / Trevor — attaching the items we discussed: rotation-checklist.pdf (mapping + SOC 2 appendix), key-eviction-log.csv (sample, redacted), handshake-trace-sample.log.  

Notes on the CSV export format: 
- event_ts: ISO8601 UTC timestamps
- key_id_hash: SHA256 of the key identifier (non-reversible, used so auditors can assert consistency across events)
- key_version: integer
- action: REVOKE | EVICT | DELETE | ROTATE
- reason_code: EVICT-ROT (rotation), EVICT-COMP (compromise detection), EVICT-MAN (manual admin eviction)
- tenant_id_redacted: tenant-XXXX (we replaced real tenant ids)

Retention: hot logs retained 90 days; index metadata stored 7 years. Raw unredacted logs are available under an enterprise NDA export. Eviction behavior: automatic eviction is only triggered by our compromise detection rule set (anomalous access patterns + KMS integrity check) — routine rotations are performed as scheduled and are labeled ROTATE / EVICT-ROT in the logs.

Handshake trace explanation: The sample log includes the application-level KMSWrap/KMSUnwrap entries and a TLS negotiated cipher line; we removed any session secrets. You can verify authenticity via the manifest hash (SHA256) included in the rotation-checklist.pdf.

Attachments included: rotation-checklist.pdf (2pg), key-eviction-log.csv (sample, 120 rows), handshake-trace-sample.log (1 trace).

If auditors want a signature/attestation from our KeyOps engineer (timestamp + signature file), we can produce an HSM-signed hash.

Irene Choi
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
